title: Hector meets Andromache
intro: Hector finds his wife and infant son at the gate. Watch the household vocabulary and the contrast between the child's two names.

notes.text: ὀτρηρός, active / diligent; ταμίη, housekeeper or stewardess, fem of ταμίης.
ἄνωγα, command: 2sg perf with pres sense; μυθέομαι aor mid inf, tell / relate.
ἀληθής, neut acc pl used as a noun: the truth; object of μυθήσασθαι.
γαλόως, husband's sister; εἰνάτηρ, husband's brother's wife: gen pl, with houses understood after ἐς.
ἐξοίχομαι 3sg pres, has gone out; ἱλάσκομαι 3pl pres, propitiate, with acc of deity.
οὕνεκα, because; τείρω pres pass inf, be hard pressed. Τρῶας is its acc subject in reported news.
Neut noun, strength / mastery / victory; here the Achaeans have the upper hand.
ἐπείγομαι pres mid ptc, hastening; ἀφικάνω 3sg pres, arrives. Vivid present in the report.
μαίνομαι pres mid ptc, dat sg fem; ἔοικα perf ptc, nom sg fem: resembling a woman distraught. Resemblance takes dat.
Nurse; specifically the attendant carrying the baby.
ἠμί 3sg impf, said; ἀποσεύομαι 3sg root aor mid, rushed away. Very different stems from ordinary λέγω / τρέχω.
ἀγυιά, street: acc pl after κατά, along.
εὖτε, when; διέξειμι pres inf, go out through. Epic -μεναι; dependent on ἔμελλε.
τῇ, by which way; πεδίον δέ = πεδίονδε, toward the plain, with directional -δε.
πολύδωρος, richly dowered; θέω pres ptc fem, running. ἐναντίη: to meet him.
ναίω 3sg impf, dwelt; ὑλήεις, wooded: dat sg fem agreeing with Πλάκῳ, the mountain Placus.
Thebe beneath Placus, in Asia Minor; not Boeotian Thebes. Dat of place with the preceding ὑπό phrase.
Κίλικες dat pl in -εσσι; ἀνάσσω pres ptc, ruling, with dat of the people ruled.
ἔχω 3sg impf mid, elided ἔχετο: was married to Hector; dat of husband.
ἀντάω 3sg aor, met, with dat οἱ; κίω 3sg impf, went. ἀμφίπολος: attendant.
κόλπος, bosom / fold of clothing; ἀταλάφρων, tender-minded, acc sg of the baby.
νήπιος, infant / uncomprehending; αὔτως, simply / just: a mere little child.
Ἑκτορίδης, son of Hector; ἀλίγκιος, resembling, with dat ἀστέρι. Both acc sg modifying παῖδα.
καλέω iterative impf 3sg: used to call. -σκ- marks repeated or customary action.
Scamandrius recalls Troy's river Scamander; Astyanax means lord of the city, honoring his father's protection of Troy.
οἶος, alone; ἐρύομαι 3sg impf, guarded / defended. Distinguish ἐρύω, draw / drag.
μειδάω 3sg aor, smiled; παρίστημι 3sg impf mid, stood beside. σιωπῇ: silently.
ἐμφύω 3sg root aor, split by intervening words: clasped / clung to his hand. οἱ possessive dat; χειρί dat after ἐν.
Affectionate but distressed address, “dear, strange man”; φθίω 3sg fut active, will destroy. Subject τὸ σὸν μένος, your own fighting spirit.
ἐλεαίρω 2sg pres, pity / have compassion for; objects continue on the next page.
